Finally, for those urban areas which have experienced extreme population growth in the suburbs as compared to the city and where unusual circumstances exist, the individual determination option is available.

Inasmuch as we believe that the above formula reflects the trend of modern expansion of urban areas and generally demarcates the area conforming to the present-day meaning of "adjacent to and commercially a part of" the base municipality, we adopt this scheme as the new population-mileage formula. We take this action cognizant of the fact that this general rule will not describe all commercial zones with precision, yet at the same time we are convinced that the above formula represents a workable method of prescribing reasonable bounds for contemporary commercial zones. Transportation movements of even 15 or 20 miles beyond city limits do not contradict modern notions of "local movements" in large metropolitan areas. Metropolitan transportation networks of beltways and expressways often span such an area, and these distances can be covered in a matter of minutes.
